title: Shiloh
summary: Shiloh is a central-highland site portrayed in Joshua, Judges, and 1 Samuel as an assembly, allotment, sanctuary, festival, and priestly center; Psalms and Jeremiah later remember its abandonment as a warning.
historical_context: Shiloh is commonly identified with Khirbet Seilun north of Bethel. Excavation documents a long occupation sequence including Iron I remains, but no excavated feature securely proves the location of the tent of meeting or an event narrated in Judges or Samuel.
ancient_near_east_context: The site lies within the central highland road network. Judges 21's route description relative to Bethel, Lebonah, and the main road presents Shiloh as a recognizable regional gathering place rather than an unspecified sacred symbol.
hebraic_worldview: Shiloh joins sacred presence, sacrifice, priestly responsibility, festival, and tribal assembly. Its later canonical use also insists that a revered sanctuary does not guarantee protection when covenant conduct is corrupt.
canonical_context: Joshua places the tent of meeting and land allotment at Shiloh; Judges mentions the house of God and an annual festival; 1 Samuel narrates worship, priestly corruption, revelation, and the ark's loss; Psalm 78 and Jeremiah 7 turn Shiloh into a warning for Jerusalem.
literary_context: Shiloh's role changes across the canonical sequence: assembly and allotment in Joshua, sanctuary and festival in Judges, priestly center and judgment in Samuel, and cautionary memory in Psalms and Jeremiah.
covenantal_significance: The site embodies both divine presence among the tribes and accountability at a sacred center; its remembered rejection guards against treating holy geography as immunity from judgment.
canonical_role: Shiloh connects land allotment, regional worship, Samuel's call, the ark crisis, and prophetic warnings about presuming on sacred space.

related_objects.notes: Joshua 18 locates the tent of meeting and land allotment at Shiloh.
Judges 18 and 21 name Shiloh's house of God and annual festival setting.
The evidence cluster separates textual sanctuary claims from excavated occupation.
First Samuel locates Samuel's childhood, call, and early ministry at Shiloh.

scripture_references.notes: Tent of meeting, tribal assembly, survey, and allotment at Shiloh.
The Danite image is temporally compared with the house of God at Shiloh.
Annual festival and precise route description for Shiloh.
Sanctuary, priesthood, Samuel's call, ark loss, and judgment.
Shiloh is invoked as a warning against confidence in Jerusalem's temple.

interpretive_notes.note: Iron I occupation at Shiloh provides site context but does not identify the tent of meeting, the house of God, or the festival of Judges 21 archaeologically.
Jeremiah's appeal to Shiloh is a theological use of remembered sanctuary judgment, not evidence that every detail of Shiloh's earlier history can be reconstructed from Jeremiah.
